focus: Data visualization, statistics, statistical analysis, and reproducible scientific computing
title: From CSV Rows to Trustworthy Results: Command-Line Statistics That Travel
utility_title: csv-profile: Quick Structural and Numeric Checks for CSV Data
utility_use_case: A researcher receives a new instrument export before plotting trends. They run `bash csv-profile.sh --file measurements.csv` to see whether the rows match the header, where blank cells occur, and which columns contain finite numeric values. A nonzero exit due to ragged rows can stop a downstream pipeline, while the JSON report offers a quick, reproducible checkpoint before the researcher investigates repairs and applies domain-specific rules.

source.book_label: Hands-On Data Science with the Command Line - Automate -- Jason Morris; Chris McCubbin; Raymond Page

generation.estimate_note: Standard uncached token estimate; cache writes, discounts, and actual billing can differ.

editorial_review.summary: Corrected CSV record numbering and clarified error handling and floating-point overflow limits in the utility documentation.

edits.old: A row with a different field count is reported by its one-based file line number, counting the header as line 1.
edits.new: A row with a different field count is reported by its one-based CSV record number, counting the header as record 1; quoted newlines do not increase this number.

edits.old: Input and validation errors are reported by the command-line parser and also produce a nonzero exit.
edits.new: File-access, decoding, and validation errors caught by the program are reported by the command-line parser and produce a nonzero exit.

edits.old: This is a screening profile, not a schema validator or repair tool.
edits.new: This is a screening profile, not a schema validator or repair tool; sufficiently large finite values can overflow the floating-point total and prevent a JSON report.
